text: PRE-REGISTERED RESULT (plan hash cd955b3977b5, frozen before any prediction). n=15 of 17 planned; the 2 losses were salts whose multi-component SMILES the affinity head rejected, a data-prep defect since fixed by adding desalting. PRIMARY: Spearman rho = 0.3036 with bootstrap 95% CI [-0.3285, 0.7658], Holm p = 0.81407. The interval spans zero, so H1 (ranking ability) is FALSIFIED: on this set the affinity head shows no demonstrated ability to rank AChE inhibitor potency.

H2 (memorization signature) FALSIFIED. Spearman(|error|, ChEMBL record count) = 0.074, i.e. essentially zero. Position A predicted that error would be smaller for heavily assayed compounds; it is not. IMPORTANT LIMIT: this falsifies the SIGNATURE tested, not memorization itself. Independent forensics replicated Boltz-2's published ChEMBL extraction predicate and found five assays containing huperzine A x AChE that pass every enumerable filter, so the pair is PROBABLY IN the training data. Record count is a weak proxy, and n=15 has little power to detect a modest correlation.

H3 CONFIRMED: the disputed huperzine A error is REPRESENTATIVE, not an outlier. Its absolute error 2.4086 log sits at z = 0.94 against a set mean of 1.3593 log. The method's typical error on this set is about 1.4 log units, so the single observation was neither cherry-picked nor anomalous — it was ordinary.

REFERENCE-QUALITY LIMITATION, measured. 13 of the 17 benchmark reference values rest on a SINGLE ChEMBL record, because build_target_corpus draws a flat activity budget across the whole target rather than retrieving every record per compound. Verified for huperzine A: ChEMBL holds 23 IC50 records for this pair spanning 3.99 log10 units (0.54 to 5280 nM, median 47 nM), and the single record captured (5.0 nM) sits at the 17th percentile. Measured against the median instead, the model's error falls from 2.41 to 1.43 log. So roughly 40% of the headline discrepancy was an artifact of which literature value happened to be retrieved.

CONSEQUENCE. The published inter-laboratory reproducibility floor for public IC50 data is sigma = 0.68 log (Kalliokoski et al., PLoS ONE 8:e61007, 2013), and for this specific pair the in-situ floor computed from 253 pairwise literature comparisons is sigma ~ 0.99 log. The study's mean absolute error is 1.36 log. Model error and reference error are therefore the same order of magnitude, and this study cannot separate them. That is the honest ceiling on what it establishes.

note: reference noise limits what the primary metric can show
